## About

AI Client is a desktop and web application for working with AI models on your own computer. It speaks the OpenAI Responses API and the Chat Completions fallback, so it works with OpenAI, Azure, local models, and any other provider that follows the same protocol.

Everything runs locally. A small Host process stores your projects, chat history, and credentials, and the Blazor WebAssembly UI renders in your browser or in the desktop shell. Tools reach the model through MCP (Model Context Protocol), so the assistant can read, edit, search, and run commands in directories you grant.

## Features

- **Streaming chat with Markdown** — see the response as it is generated, with rendered code blocks, tables, and safe links.
- **Git-like branching** — fork any message into a new branch to try a different path without losing the original.
- **Local MCP tools** — give the model access to files, search, and other tools, with per-project policies and confirmation prompts.
- **Multiple providers** — connect to several endpoints and pick a model per chat. Credentials stay on your machine.
- **Projects with isolation** — each project has its own endpoint, MCP servers, file system roots, and system prompt.
- **Cross-platform** — Chrome or Edge on any OS, a native desktop app for Windows, macOS, and Linux, or install the web app from your browser.

## Getting started

1. Open **[ai.dev-team.org](https://ai.dev-team.org/)** in Chrome or Edge.
2. Download the local Host for your platform, or pick a desktop installer for Windows, macOS, or Linux.
3. Create a project, add your endpoint and credential, allow a directory, and start chatting.

The Host is a small background process that holds your data. Close it when you are done; your projects and history stay in the local data directory.

C# scripting tools (`AI.Mcp.CSharp`) are optional. Select **C# scripting tools** in the Windows or macOS Host/Desktop installer. On Linux, install the companion `AI.Mcp.CSharp-<runtime>.deb` package alongside Host or Desktop, in either order. The scripting server includes its own .NET runtime.

Build the installers on the matching operating system with `dotnet run --project build -- package-release --runtime win-x64 --version 1.0.0` (also supports `win-arm64`, `osx-x64`, `osx-arm64`, `linux-x64`, and `linux-arm64`). Output is in `artifacts/release/packages`; Windows packaging requires Inno Setup 6, macOS uses `pkgbuild`/`productbuild`, and Linux uses `dpkg-deb`.
